preconditions.description: The number of strings in the list A is between 1 and 30 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(s) <= 100 for s in A)
preconditions.description: Each string in the list A has length between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) for s in A)
preconditions.description: All elements in the list A are strings.

postconditions.expression: result == sum(f(L) for L in nonempty_contiguous_sublists(A))
postconditions.description: The output is the sum of f(L) for all nonempty contiguous sublists L of A, where f(L) is 1 if L is stable and 0 otherwise.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= f(L) <= 1 for L in nonempty_contiguous_sublists(A))
postconditions.description: For each nonempty contiguous sublist L, f(L) is either 0 or 1.

postconditions.expression: is_stable(L) == (all(is_good(message, L) for message in generate_messages(L)))
postconditions.description: A list L is stable if and only if every message in S_L (the set of all messages constructible from L) is good.
A message is good if and only if the number of its cyclic shifts that are in S_L equals the number of strings (k) used to construct it.

postconditions.expression: count_good_cyclic_shifts(message, L) == len({cyclic_shift(message, i) for i in range(len(message)) if cyclic_shift(message, i) in S_L})
postconditions.description: The count of good cyclic shifts is the number of unique cyclic shifts of the message that are in S_L.
